title: LSEG (Refinitiv) SDC Platinum: Joint Ventures & Alliances (JV&A) module
author_source: LSEG Data & Analytics, deals database, 2024 (migrated to Workspace 1 Jan 2024)
note: Standard alliance database in IB and strategy: roughly 77,700 formal joint ventures and 216,000 strategic alliances worldwide (SDC marketing figures), deal-level records with participant names, nations, SIC codes, alliance type flags (JV, R&D, licensing, marketing, manufacturing, supply), equity stakes, announcement/termination dates, deal synopsis. Since 2024 delivered through the LSEG Workspace Excel add-in (unlimited downloads) and via WRDS as the SDC JV&A component. Known under-coverage of announced alliances (Schilling 2009, SMJ 30(3)); coverage years to check (historically from mid-1980s/1990).
relevance: Core alliance-level and dyad-level data: partner nationality and activity-type flags allow coding of which functions partners integrate (scope) and how deeply (equity vs. non-equity), i.e. a direct operationalisation of differentiated integration across partners and activities; can be merged with country-level distance measures. Access: WU licence via WRDS/LSEG Workspace (check whether the WU WRDS subscription includes the SDC JV&A component).

title: WRDS at WU Wien: Compustat Global, Orbis (via WRDS), SDC and other modules
author_source: WU Library / WRDS, database access page, 2026
note: WU's WRDS access page: scientific staff, guest researchers, external lecturers and regular students can request personal WRDS accounts. Compustat Global offers fundamentals and market data for 40,000+ non-North-American listed firms from 1979 onwards (daily updates); Orbis data are also available through WRDS. The exact list of WU-licensed WRDS modules (e.g. whether SDC JV&A is included) must be checked on the page.
relevance: Firm-level control and performance variables (size, R&D intensity, segment data, international sales) for alliance partners identified in SDC/Zephyr; needed for firm-level moderators in models of partner-specific integration depth. Access: WU licence (personal WRDS account).

title: Zephyr / Orbis M&A (Bureau van Dijk - Moody's): M&A, IPO and joint-venture deals
author_source: Bureau van Dijk - Moody's Analytics, deals database, WU access page 2026
note: Around one million completed or announced transactions (M&A, IPOs, joint ventures, private equity, MBI/MBO) with integrated BvD company financials; worldwide coverage for the last ten years, deals with European or American participation back to 1997; hourly updates; English interface. At WU accessible on campus, remote access for WU employees and (until further notice) regular students. Now branded Orbis M&A at some institutions.
relevance: Second alliance/JV deal source to triangulate SDC coverage (JV deal type with partner ownership percentages and BvD IDs that link to Orbis ownership trees), allowing measurement of equity differentiation among JV partners and partner-level country attributes. Access: WU licence.

title: Orbis (Bureau van Dijk - Moody's): company, ownership and subsidiary data worldwide
author_source: Bureau van Dijk - Moody's Analytics, company database, WU access page 2026
note: Information on about 580 million companies worldwide, 48 million with detailed financials; standardised consolidated and unconsolidated statements, ratios, managers, stock prices, detailed shareholder/subsidiary links (ownership trees), industry reports, Zephyr M&A deals and patents. Accessible on the WU campus; Orbis data also via WRDS for WU staff and students with WRDS accounts. Related WU products: Orbis Europe (143 million European firms), Orbis Bank Focus.
relevance: Identifies jointly owned subsidiaries (JVs) and their ownership splits across countries, building a partner-by-country matrix of equity integration; also provides partner-level controls. Access: WU licence (campus / WRDS).

title: Orbis Crossborder Investment (Bureau van Dijk): greenfield FDI projects and cross-border deals
author_source: Bureau van Dijk - Moody's Analytics, FDI project database, WU access page 2026
note: Covers foreign direct investment projects (greenfield and expansion), cross-border deals and information on the participating companies, with source and destination countries, sector, investment value and job estimates; coverage years to check on the WU page.
relevance: Lets the researcher contrast alliance-based entry (SDC/Zephyr) with wholly owned FDI in the same country pairs, i.e. whether firms differentiate integration mode by destination; project-level location data support country-pair fixed effects. Access: WU licence.

title: Crunchbase (academic research access programme and data licence)
author_source: Crunchbase, company and funding database, licence page 2026
note: Company, investor, funding-round, acquisition and partnership records for start-ups and tech firms worldwide; the licence allows internal research and publication of aggregate statistics; free or subsidised access for graduate-level academic research on application (case-by-case). The OECD STI working paper 2017/08 'Using Crunchbase for economic and managerial research' documents coverage and biases. Not confirmed as a WU library subscription.
relevance: Source for technology and platform partnerships of younger firms not captured by SDC; useful for alliance portfolios in tech/pharma ecosystems and for identifying regional partner clusters. Access: free for approved academic research, otherwise paid.

title: EUDIFF1 and EUDIFF2: Differentiated European Integration datasets (treaty law 1952-2020; secondary law 1958-2018)
author_source: Schimmelfennig and Winzen, dataset page, 2020 (OUP book 'Ever Looser Union?')
note: EUDIFF1 starts from every EU treaty article in force in each year 1952-2020 and codes whether each member state is legally exempted or excluded (opt-outs, enhanced cooperation, accession transition periods). EUDIFF2 codes differentiation in EU secondary legislation 1958-2018 (member-state-year-act level). Funded by SNSF/DFG (DACH 'Differentiated Integration in Europe') and H2020 InDivEU. Dataset page notes that the full datasets had not yet been publicly released; an earlier EUDIFF2 version (1958-2012, Duttle et al. 2017 JEPP) is on the ETH Research Collection. Contact the authors for access.
relevance: The reference measurement model for differentiated integration: country-year counts of exemptions by policy area are the template for coding partner-specific exemptions, opt-outs and tiers within multi-partner alliances; also usable directly as a country-level 'integration-depth' covariate for EU-based alliance partners. Access: free on request / to check.

title: ETH Zurich European Politics group: dataset page (EUDIFF2 secondary-law differentiation 1958-2012, Duttle et al. 2017, and related EU datasets)
author_source: ETH Zurich European Politics, dataset listing; Duttle et al., JEPP 24(3), 2017
note: Dataset page of the Schimmelfennig group listing downloadable datasets, including the EUDIFF2 data and codebook used in Duttle et al. (2017) 'Opting out from European Union legislation: the differentiation of secondary law' (all exemptions granted to member states in secondary law 1958-2012, by act, member state and policy area). The Konstanz partner project page (Holzinger) documents the DACH project 'Differentiated Integration in Europe'.
relevance: Provides the publicly released version of the secondary-law differentiation data plus codebook, i.e. a worked example of how to code 'who is exempted from what, for how long' that can be adapted to alliance agreements (e.g. partner-specific carve-outs in airline JVs). Access: free.

title: InDivEU integrated database and datasets on differentiated integration (uses of DI, public opinion, flexible implementation)
outlet: Integrating Diversity in the European Union (H2020)
author_source: InDivEU / EUI, H2020 project 2019-2021, data outputs
note: The H2020 InDivEU project (14 partners, coordinated by the EUI's European Governance and Politics Programme) published two databases on the uses of differentiated integration and two datasets on public opinion and flexible implementation, plus an integrated database on preferences of citizens, parties, governments and stakeholders towards DI, and explainer pages ('What is differentiated integration?', 'When and how to use DI?').
relevance: Country-level preference and usage measures for DI among EU states; the explainer material offers a concise typology (multi-speed, variable geometry, à la carte, external differentiation) transferable to alliance tiers (full member, connecting partner, metal-neutral JV). Access: free.

title: Berry, Guillén and Zhou cross-national distance data (nine dimensions; 2023 update to 2021)
outlet: Wharton Lauder Institute / Heather Berry data page
author_source: Berry, Guillén and Zhou, JIBS 41(9) 2010; data update 2023
note: Longitudinal dyadic distance data for nine dimensions (economic, financial, political, administrative, cultural, demographic, knowledge, global connectedness, geographic) for a large set of country pairs; December 2017 and 2023 updates (the 2023 version covers most dimensions to 2021); download instructions on the Wharton management department site; users must cite Berry, Guillén and Zhou (2010). Complementary tools: NYU Stern Globalization Explorer CAGE Comparator (Ghemawat; 163 countries, 65 industries, 16 distance types) at globalization.stern.nyu.edu/cage.
relevance: The standard set of country-pair distance covariates for alliance research; lets the study test whether partners differentiate integration depth by dyadic distance (e.g. deeper integration with institutionally close partners), matching the EU 'distance to core' logic. Access: free with citation.

title: DESTA: Design of Trade Agreements database (version 2.3, September 2025)
publisher: University of Salzburg / McGill / World Trade Institute Bern
author_source: Dür, Baccini and Elsig, Review of International Organizations 9(3) 2014; DESTA v2.3, 2025
note: Systematic coding of about 846 preferential trade agreements signed since 1945: list of treaties (CSV/XLSX), dyadic treaty list, content coding of 100+ design items (depth, flexibility, dispute settlement, non-trade issues, IPR, environment) with codebook. Best New Dataset Award (IPES 2017). Free download.
relevance: Country-pair 'formal economic integration' control: whether and how deeply two partners' home countries are tied by a PTA, which conditions cross-border alliance scope; the depth-flexibility coding (Baccini, Dür and Elsig, ISQ 2015) is also a design template for coding alliance contracts. Access: free.

title: OECD FDI Regulatory Restrictiveness Index (FDI RRI)
author_source: OECD, indicator dataset, 2025 edition (measures in force end-2024)
note: Scores statutory FDI restrictions in four categories (foreign equity limits, screening/approval, key personnel, operational restrictions) for 100+ economies and 22 sectors, yearly from 1997 (selected years) to 2024; downloadable CSV/XLSX/XML from the OECD Data Explorer ('OECD FDI Regulatory Restrictiveness Index - Scores'); the 2024 policy paper summarises trends.
relevance: Country-sector restrictiveness explains why firms integrate via minority JVs rather than acquisitions in certain host countries, i.e. a policy driver of differentiated integration across alliance partners' home markets; sector detail (air transport is a scored sector) matters for airline alliances. Access: free.

title: Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI 2.0, estimates 1996-2025)
author_source: World Bank WGI project, annual dataset, 2026 release
note: Six composite governance dimensions (voice and accountability, political stability, government effectiveness, regulatory quality, rule of law, control of corruption) for 200+ economies, 1996-2025; the 2025 methodological review (WGI 2.0) revised source screening and aggregation; Excel/Stata downloads, WGI calculator and a reproducibility package on the World Bank Reproducible Research Repository.
relevance: Standard institutional-quality measures for computing institutional distance between alliance partners' countries (Kogut-Singh-type index on WGI) and for host-country risk; a typical regressor for partner-specific integration depth. Access: free (CC BY 4.0).

title: UNCTAD FDI statistics (UNCTADstat and World Investment Report annex tables, 1990-2024)
author_source: UNCTAD, statistical database and WIR annex tables, 2025
note: FDI inflows, outflows, inward and outward stocks by region and economy 1990-2024 (Excel annex tables and UNCTADstat), plus cross-border M&A and greenfield project tables in the World Investment Report; bilateral FDI series (2001-2012) are no longer published online and can be requested from fdistat@unctad.org. Free, no registration.
relevance: Country-level integration into global investment flows as a context variable; bilateral stocks (on request) measure how economically integrated two partner countries already are, a proxy for the 'baseline' integration against which alliance differentiation is measured. Access: free.

title: Hofstede dimension data matrix (six national culture dimensions, version 2015-12-08)
author_source: Hofstede, Hofstede and Minkov, data matrix, 2015 version (Cultures and Organizations 3rd ed. 2010)
note: Country scores (0-100) on power distance, individualism, masculinity, uncertainty avoidance, long-term orientation and indulgence for roughly 100 countries and regions; downloadable in .xls, .csv, .doc and .sav; free for research without permission, commercial use on request. Alternative culture scores: GLOBE 2004 practices/values for 62 societies at globeproject.com/results.html; ESS/EVS-based European cultural distance indices (Kaasa, Vadi and Varblane 2016) at lepo.it.da.ut.ee/~akaasa/culturaldistances/.
relevance: Input for the Kogut-Singh (1988) cultural distance index between alliance partners; the most used cultural covariate in alliance governance studies and hence a natural moderator of partner-specific integration. Access: free.

title: GLOBE Project results: societal culture practices and values scores (2004 study, 62 societies; GLOBE 2020 programme)
authors: GLOBE Project (House, Robert J. et al.; Dorfman, Peter; Javidan, Mansour)
author_source: GLOBE Project, culture and leadership study, 2004 data with 2020 programme
note: Country and country-cluster scores on nine culture dimensions, each as practices ('as is') and values ('should be'), based on 17,300 middle managers in 951 organisations across 62 societies (2004); 2014 CEO study; GLOBE 2020 (culture, trust, leadership in about 150 countries) still being finalised, with country data returned to co-investigators first. Results browsable by country online; dimension definitions and scale items downloadable.
relevance: Alternative culture distance basis to Hofstede and the only source that separates practices from values, useful for robustness of cultural-distance effects on integration depth between alliance partners. Access: free (online browsing; full GLOBE 2020 data not yet released).

title: US DOT list of active antitrust-immunized airline alliances and ATI case dockets
authors: US Department of Transportation, Office of Aviation Analysis
author_source: US DOT, regulatory list and case register, last updated 14 March 2024
note: Official list of active antitrust-immunized (ATI) alliances with docket numbers and expansion decisions (e.g. American-BA-Iberia-Finnair-Royal Jordanian DOT-OST-2008-0252; Delta-Air France-KLM-Alitalia; United-Lufthansa-Air Canada; American-Qantas DOT-OST-2018-0030; American-JAL), the DOT ATI case page and the 'Alliances and Codeshares' page describing the filing of cooperative agreements. GAO-19-237 reviews DOT's ATI process. EU counterparts: Commission commitments decisions AT.39595 (A++ Lufthansa/United/Air Canada, 2013; new proceedings opened 7 August 2024) and AT.39596 (BA/AA/Iberia, 2010) in the DG COMP case register.
relevance: Defines the deepest tier of airline alliance integration (metal-neutral, revenue-sharing JVs) with exact start dates, partners and route scope; combined with alliance membership histories it yields a partner-by-year panel of integration tiers (member, connecting partner, codeshare, ATI JV) for differentiated-integration measurement. Access: free.

title: BTS T-100 International Segment data (US and foreign carriers, traffic and capacity by nonstop segment)
publisher: US DOT Bureau of Transportation Statistics
author_source: BTS, monthly administrative data, 1990-present
note: Monthly nonstop segment data for all flights with at least one US endpoint, reported by US and foreign carriers: operating carrier, origin, destination, aircraft type, service class, passengers, freight, mail, seats, departures scheduled/performed, load factor; international data released about three months after domestic; free download via TranStats (table 'T-100 International Segment (All Carriers)').
relevance: Objective route-level outcome data for transatlantic and transpacific JVs: capacity coordination and route rationalisation can be measured before and after a partner joins an immunized JV, giving a behavioural measure of integration depth per partner pair. Access: free.

title: OAG Historical Flight Data and Cirium Diio schedules (codeshare and partner flags, 2004-present)
author_source: OAG and Cirium, commercial schedule databases, 2026
note: OAG: 20+ years (2004-present) of scheduled and actual flight records configurable by airline and airport, including codeshare information, aircraft type, delays; delivered via API or flight-leg reports; OAG master data support codeshare matching across alliance networks. Cirium Diio: 97% of worldwide scheduled flights, 20 years back and 11 months forward, with capacity, fares and traffic flows. Both commercial; academic pricing on request; not known to be in the WU library catalogue.
relevance: Codeshare and schedule-coordination intensity between every pair of alliance members over time, i.e. the actual (not formal) degree of network integration, which can differ sharply within one alliance (core JV partners vs. peripheral members). Access: paid.

title: Global Strategic Partnership (GSP) dataset, 1990-2020 (state-level strategic partnerships; Harvard Dataverse)
outlet: Harvard Dataverse / Conflict Management and Peace Science
author_source: Chang-Liao, Fu and Lin, replication dataset, 2025 (article in Conflict Management and Peace Science, 2026)
note: About 1,400 inter-state strategic partnership agreements announced 1990-2020 across 137 countries, coded by mutual recognition, formal documentation and issue scope, distinguishing partnerships from formal alliances and alignments; the introducing article shows the US trades and transfers arms more with non-allied partners than with allies.
relevance: Country-pair measure of political alignment and 'differentiated' inter-state integration below full alliance, usable as a geopolitical covariate for cross-border firm alliances (does firm-level integration follow state-level partnership tiers?). Access: free (open replication data).

title: Academy of International Business (AIB): calls for papers, JIBS/JIBP, AIB Insights, chapters
author_source: AIB, association website, 2026
note: Portal of the IB field: annual meeting calls (AIB 2027 Kuala Lumpur), the 'Global Value Chains, Networks and Operations' track covering alliances and networks, JIBS paper development workshops, the Call for Papers listing of IB special issues, AIB Insights (open access), chapter conferences (US-West, LAC, MENA 'IB in a Fractured Geopolitical World').
relevance: Entry point for positioning a differentiated-integration-in-alliances paper (track selection, special-issue calls, PDWs); AIB's own AIB-UNCTAD alliance article shows reflexive interest in alliance governance. Access: free (membership for submissions).

title: Strategic Management Society: Cooperative Strategies Interest Group
author_source: SMS, interest-group page, 2026
note: Interest group dedicated to cooperative strategies at functional, business, corporate, group and network levels: alliances, JVs, federations, constellations, networks, buyer-supplier relations, franchises, PPPs and board interlocks; aims at knowledge on antecedents, consequences, emergence, evolution and termination of cooperative arrangements; webinars, IG socials at the annual conference, online 'Circles'; the Strategic Management Explorer offers a curated 'Cooperative Strategy' topic page.
relevance: The research community for alliance governance and multi-partner constellations (Gomes-Casseres' term) where a differentiated-integration framing would be reviewed; venue for SMS Berlin 2026 track selection and co-author search. Access: free (SMS membership for full features).

title: ASAP - Association of Strategic Alliance Professionals: Handbook, State of Alliance Management studies, Strategic Alliance Quarterly
author_source: ASAP, professional association website, 2026
note: Global non-profit for alliance and partnership managers: ASAP Handbook of Alliance Management (5th edition announced for autumn 2026 with ecosystems, governance and value realisation), Research Package with the 4th-6th 'State of Alliance Management' studies and a metrics report, biopharma and IT partnering supplements, Strategic Alliance Quarterly/Monthly, certification (CA-AM, CSAP) and an AI knowledge hub ('Ally').
relevance: Practitioner benchmark data on alliance governance structures (tiered partner programmes, portfolio segmentation) that document differentiated treatment of partners in practice; potential survey partner for primary data. Access: paid membership for most reports.

title: DiCE - Differentiation: Clustering Excellence (hub for EU3D, InDivEU and EU IDEA)
authors: DiCE consortium (ARENA University of Oslo, EUI, IAI, TEPSA)
author_source: DiCE, H2020 coordination project 2020-2022, project hub
note: Clusters the three Horizon 2020 research actions on differentiation in European governance (GOVERNANCE-02-2018-2019): EU3D (Oslo), InDivEU (EUI) and EU IDEA (IAI); translates findings into policy advice (scenario marathon, policy briefs, networking conferences on Brexit).
relevance: One-stop overview of the EU differentiated-integration research programme whose concepts (multi-speed, variable geometry, external differentiation, dominance) the research question transfers to inter-firm alliances. Access: free.

title: EU IDEA - EU Integration and Differentiation for Effectiveness and Accountability
author_source: EU IDEA / IAI, H2020 project 2019-2021, project website
note: 15-partner H2020 project asking whether, how much and what form of differentiation is conducive to a more effective, cohesive and democratic EU; policy papers and research papers on EMU, CFSP, AFSJ, Brexit and external differentiation in single-market access; key finding: formal differentiation works when linked to EU institutions, clear objectives and accountability mechanisms.
relevance: Supplies the effectiveness-accountability trade-off framework for evaluating differentiated arrangements, transferable to alliance governance (when do partner-specific carve-outs improve alliance performance vs. undermine cohesion?). Access: free.

title: EU3D - EU Differentiation, Dominance and Democracy (ARENA, University of Oslo)
authors: EU3D consortium (ARENA Centre for European Studies)
author_source: EU3D / ARENA, H2020 project Feb 2019-Jul 2023, project website
note: About 50 researchers in 10 countries (coordinator John Erik Fossum) specifying when differentiation is politically acceptable, institutionally sustainable and democratically legitimate, with an explicit focus on dominance (asymmetric power among members); research paper and report series downloadable.
relevance: The dominance lens maps onto alliance asymmetry (anchor carriers vs. junior members; lead firms in multi-partner JVs) and offers hypotheses on how power asymmetry drives differentiated integration. Access: free.

title: ECPR Research Network on Differentiated Integration in the EU (RNDI)
author_source: ECPR RNDI, research network page, 2026
note: Network of about 166 scholars (steering committee chaired by Sandra Kröger, Exeter; with Cristina Fasone, Dirk Leuffen, Christopher Lord) covering empirical, legal and historical mapping of DI, public and party support, normative trade-offs and effects on states, citizens and the constitutional order; runs a seminar series and panels at ECPR General Conferences; methodologically plural and open beyond political science.
relevance: Where the DI concept community meets; a management scholar presenting an alliance application would find discussants and the ECPR 2027 Barcelona panels. Access: free.

title: EUR-Lex glossary: Enhanced cooperation (Art. 20 TEU, Arts. 326-334 TFEU)
authors: Publications Office of the European Union
author_source: EUR-Lex, legal glossary entry, current version
note: Official definition: at least nine member states may establish advanced integration in a field when the EU as a whole cannot achieve it within a reasonable period; last-resort authorisation by the Council on Commission proposal with Parliament consent; open to all member states at any time; no extension of Union competences. Related: European Parliament resolution of 17 January 2019 on differentiated integration and the 2018 EP study on implementing enhanced cooperation.
relevance: Authoritative legal description of the EU's 'opt-in core group' mechanism, the closest institutional analogue to sub-alliance JVs open to other members (e.g. oneworld's transatlantic JV open to Aer Lingus); useful for definitions in the paper. Access: free.

title: Star Alliance official site: member airlines and Connecting Partner model
author_source: Star Alliance, corporate website, 2026
note: Founded 14 May 1997 (first global alliance); 26 members (Aegean, Air Canada, Air China, Air India, Air New Zealand, ANA, Asiana, Austrian, Avianca, Brussels, Copa, Croatia, EGYPTAIR, Ethiopian, EVA, ITA, LOT, Lufthansa, Shenzhen, Singapore, South African, SWISS, TAP, THAI, Turkish, United), 5,000+ aircraft, 1,300 airports, 195 countries, 19,000+ daily departures; 'Connecting Partner' tier (Juneyao, formerly Thai Smile) requires commercial relations with only three members instead of all. Membership histories with entries/exits (e.g. SAS left for SkyTeam in 2024) documented on Wikipedia and in Skift's 'Star Alliance's 26 brands, explained'.
relevance: Primary source for the formal tier structure (member vs. connecting partner) and membership timing needed to build an alliance-member-year panel of differentiated integration. Access: free.

title: oneworld: '20 facts' page and oneworld Connect partner tier
author_source: oneworld, corporate news/facts page, 2020 (membership updated to 2025)
note: Founded 1 February 1999; now 15 members (Alaska, American, British Airways, Cathay Pacific, Finnair, Iberia, Japan Airlines, Malaysia, Qantas, Qatar, Royal Air Maroc, Royal Jordanian, SriLankan, Fiji Airways, Oman Air); 'oneworld Connect' introduced 2018 as a reduced-benefit platform for regionally focused carriers (Fiji Airways joined as Connect partner 2018 and became a full member in 2025); about 1,000 destinations in 170 countries.
relevance: Documents an explicit two-tier membership model and a partner's upgrade path from partial to full integration, a clean case of multi-speed integration inside a multi-partner alliance. Access: free.

title: SkyTeam: History of the airline alliance
authors: SkyTeam Airline Alliance Management Coöperatie U.A.
author_source: SkyTeam, corporate history page, 2026
note: Founded June 2000 by Aeroméxico, Air France, Delta and Korean Air; 18 full members today (including SAS since 2024); page gives the chronology of member entries and departures (e.g. Continental left in 2009 after the United merger) and of SkyTeam Cargo.
relevance: Third official membership chronology to complete the alliance-member-year panel; SkyTeam combines full membership with the deep Delta-Air France-KLM-Virgin Atlantic JV (341 daily transatlantic flights), illustrating a core-periphery pattern. Access: free.

title: US DOT Office of Aviation Analysis: Alliances and Codeshares (cooperative agreements review)
author_source: US DOT, policy page, current
note: Explains that US carriers must file cooperative service agreements (reciprocal codesharing, joint frequent-flyer and lounge access, joint marketing) with DOT before implementation; DOT reviews for public harm rather than approving; summarises the 1990s Office of Aviation Analysis studies that underpin the policy of encouraging international alliances.
relevance: Regulatory background for the three-tier integration ladder (codeshare filing, alliance membership, ATI joint venture) and pointer to filed agreements usable as primary documents on the scope of each partnership. Access: free.

title: Why differentiation is now at the heart of Europe's political system
authors: EUROPP - LSE European Politics and Policy blog
author_source: EUROPP blog post, 17 October 2023 (also republished by PubAffairs Bruxelles)
note: Argues that differentiation, an established cornerstone of the EU's architecture since the 1990s, has become bi-directional (more and less integration at once) and now structures the whole political system, including external differentiation with non-members (EEA, Switzerland, UK) and candidate countries.
relevance: Short, citable statement of the current DI debate; its 'bi-directional differentiation' idea parallels alliances where some members deepen into JVs while others loosen to codeshare-only ties. Access: free.

title: Flexible Europe: Differentiated integration, fairness, and democracy
author_source: Bellamy, Kröger and Lorimer, EUROPP blog, 11 February 2022 (based on their 2022 Bristol University Press book)
note: Defines DI as letting some member states pursue closer integration in specified areas without all participating, and sets out normative criteria (fair terms of cooperation, non-domination, democratic authorisation) that differentiation must meet to count as fair and democratic.
relevance: Provides the fairness criteria that can be turned into governance hypotheses for alliances: differentiated integration is stable when non-participating partners are not dominated and retain voice; useful for discussion sections. Access: free (LSE Research Online copy).

title: Pioneers Wanted: On the Differentiated Integration Pathways Towards a Genuine European Defence Union
author_source: Verfassungsblog post, 2025 (date to check)
note: Compares three legal pathways for a core group of 'able, willing and trustworthy' states: enhanced cooperation (Art. 20 TEU), a PESCO 2.0 permanent structured cooperation, and Schengen-style intergovernmental agreements later incorporated into the Treaties; notes the Lisbon Treaty removed the Nice-era exclusion of defence from enhanced cooperation. Related Verfassungsblog pieces cover 'reinforced cooperation' for NextGenEU without Poland and Hungary and the pitfalls of enhanced cooperation in the EPPO.
relevance: Legal-institutional menu of ways to form a deeper sub-group inside a larger club, directly analogous to alliance members forming a JV inside Star Alliance or oneworld; good for theorising 'pathways to differentiated integration' in alliances. Access: free (open access).

title: CAPA Airlines in Transition report, Part 1: The natural history of airline alliances
publisher: CAPA - Centre for Aviation (Aviation Week Network)
author_source: CAPA analysis report, 2013 (with 2026 follow-ups: 'Global aviation's new divide - partnership power or independence?')
note: Industry analysis of the evolution of global alliances from codeshares to multilateral groupings and then to metal-neutral, antitrust-immunised joint ventures that bypass or sit on top of alliance structures; argues alliances persist but in combination with deeper bilateral JVs. CAPA's 2026 Berlin Airline Leader Summit session and 'Aviation in 2026' outlook revisit the partnership-versus-independence divide amid geopolitical realignment.
relevance: Industry narrative of the layering of integration tiers in airline alliances, the empirical setting most suited to a differentiated-integration study; CAPA's analysis archive also documents JV formation dates. Access: paid (CAPA membership; some articles free).

title: Why Do Airlines Establish Transatlantic Joint Ventures?
author_source: Simple Flying explainer, 2024 (year to check)
note: Explains the three transatlantic JV blocs: Delta-Air France-KLM-Virgin Atlantic (341 daily flights, about 23% of transatlantic capacity), American-British Airways-Iberia-Finnair (with Aer Lingus joining), United-Lufthansa-Swiss-Austrian-Brussels-Air Canada (A++); describes revenue sharing, joint pricing, schedule coordination and the rationale on fiercely competitive North Atlantic routes. Simple Flying's 'joint venture' tag page tracks new JVs and expansions (e.g. the 2026 Southwest-Turkish partnership).
relevance: Accessible map of which alliance members belong to the deepest integration tier and which do not (e.g. Star Alliance members outside A++), i.e. the raw material for coding within-alliance differentiation. Access: free.

title: Star Alliance's 26 Brands, Explained
author_source: Skift airline analysis, 13 April 2023
note: Member-by-member profile of Star Alliance carriers, their ownership groups (Lufthansa Group's multiple members), hub roles and partnership depth; Skift also covered the EU's 2013 approval of the Lufthansa-United transatlantic venture and reports on alliance exits and entries.
relevance: Shows heterogeneity among members of the same alliance (group-owned clusters vs. stand-alone carriers), supporting a within-alliance measure of integration tiers. Access: free (some Skift Pro content paid).

title: Alliance Strategy (alliancestrategy.com): Ben Gomes-Casseres' managerial articles and blog on alliances, constellations and Star Alliance
author_source: Gomes-Casseres, personal research and blog site, ongoing
note: Collected HBR and other managerial pieces by the author of 'The Alliance Revolution' (1996), 'Mastering Alliance Strategy' (2003) and 'Remix Strategy' (2015), including 'How to Manage Multiple Partnerships', 'Managing High-Stakes Partners', 'Strategy Must Lie at the Heart of Alliances' and the Star Alliance 2000 teaching case, which analyses governance of a multi-partner constellation.
relevance: Constellation theory is the strategy literature's closest counterpart to differentiated integration (uneven ties among members of a group); the Star Alliance case and 'remix' laws give concepts for how much to integrate with which partner. Access: free.

title: How Better Contracts Can Strengthen Strategic Partnerships (HBR IdeaCast with Oliver Hart, Kate Vitasek and David Frydlinger)
author_source: HBR podcast episode, October 2025, with the authors of 'A New Approach to Contracts' (HBR 2019)
note: Nobel laureate Oliver Hart and co-authors argue for relational, principle-based contracts (fairness, reciprocity, loyalty) rather than exhaustive transactional contracts for long-term strategic partnerships; discusses how partners design governance that adapts to unforeseen contingencies. Related HBR pieces: 'How Partners Shape Strategy' (Greve, Rowley, Shipilov 2013) on tailoring alliance networks; 'How to Choose the Right Ecosystem Partners' (2022).
relevance: Contract-design perspective on why partners agree different depths of commitment with different counterparts; relational contracting is one explanation of differentiated integration within portfolios. Access: free (HBR registration limits).

title: The State of Alliance Management in 2024 and Beyond
author_source: BDO survey report / insight article, 2024
note: Survey-based practitioner report: alliances drove about one third of company revenue over the past five years; 62% of respondents say most or a great deal of their innovation comes from third-party collaboration; discusses governance maturity, metrics and portfolio segmentation of partners.
relevance: Current practitioner evidence that firms formally segment alliance portfolios into tiers with different governance intensity, i.e. differentiated integration as a managed design choice; useful for motivation and practical relevance sections. Access: free.

title: Podcast: Differentiated integration in the European Union - Frank Schimmelfennig (ACCESS EUROPE)
author_source: ACCESS EUROPE lecture podcast with Frank Schimmelfennig, 2016 (related DI podcast on the same site)
note: Lecture/podcast series by the leading DI scholar: 'The EU in crisis. Comparing integration in the euro and refugee crisis' (27 Oct 2016) and a companion podcast on differentiated integration; Schimmelfennig also teaches a College of Europe course 'Differentiated European Integration: Patterns, Causes and Institutional Design' (2025-26) and a YouTube lecture 'Development and Patterns of Differentiated Integration'.
relevance: Audio introduction to the causal theory of DI (interdependence, politicisation, heterogeneity of preferences and capacities) whose variables map onto alliance partner heterogeneity. Access: free.

title: AIB 2027 Annual Meeting, Kuala Lumpur (Sunway University), 26-30 June 2027 - call for papers opens 9 November 2026
author_source: AIB, conference call announcement, 2026 (Program Chair Grazia Santangelo)
note: Theme invites reassessment of core IB theoretical frameworks; welcomes empirical and conceptual work drawing on IB, global strategy, dynamic capabilities, microfoundations, ecosystems and behavioural IB, with contributions integrating economics, political science, sociology, history and geography especially encouraged; submissions open 9 November 2026 (deadline to check, usually mid-January); 'Global Value Chains, Networks and Operations' track covers alliances and networks.
relevance: Best-fit conference: a differentiated-integration framing imports political-science theory into IB alliance research, exactly the interdisciplinary reassessment the 2027 theme asks for; JIBS PDW usually attached. Access: AIB membership and registration.

title: EIBA 2026, 52nd Annual Conference, Aalborg, 10-13 December 2026: 'Sustainable International Business and Social Value in a Fickle World'
author_source: EIBA, conference call for submissions, 2026
note: Competitive papers (up to 10,000 words) and interactive papers (up to 6,000 words) in all IB areas; paper and panel deadline was 15 July 2026, posters, doctoral events and PDWs 1 September 2026 (passed); conference attendance and the EIBA 2027 call (location on eiba.org 'Future Conferences') remain relevant.
relevance: European IB venue with strong alliance and JV tradition (JIBS/JWB editors present); attending Aalborg 2026 to scout the 2027 call and PDWs for an early-stage differentiated-integration paper. Access: registration fee.

title: Academy of Management 87th Annual Meeting, Vienna, 30 July - 3 August 2027 (IM and STR divisions)
author_source: AOM, future meetings page and 2027 update, 2026
note: AOM moved its 2027 meeting from the US to Vienna (Austria Center Vienna and WU campus), expecting 14,000+ attendees and 4,000+ sessions; submission deadline expected in the second week of January 2027 (the 2026 deadline was 13 January); IM and STR divisions host alliance and inter-organisational relations papers and PDWs; the AOM Annals Idea Development Workshop is also scheduled in Vienna.
relevance: Home-turf conference for a WU researcher; IM division symposium on 'differentiated integration in alliances' bridging EU studies and IB would be timely; also an occasion to host EU-studies scholars at WU. Access: AOM membership and registration.

title: SMS 46th Annual Conference, Berlin, 17-20 October 2026: 'Strategy in a Fragmented Geo-Economic Landscape'
author_source: SMS, annual conference page, 2026
note: Theme 'Strategy in a Fragmented Geo Economic Landscape: Bridging Divides Across Markets, Institutions, and Technology' at the InterContinental Berlin; proposal deadline was 18 February 2026 (passed), registration open; Cooperative Strategies IG track and socials; the SMS 2027 annual conference call will follow the same cycle (proposals due mid-February 2027; location on strategicmanagement.net).
relevance: Geo-economic fragmentation is the macro driver of differentiated integration in cross-border alliances; Berlin 2026 is the place to test the framing with the Cooperative Strategies community before a 2027 submission and a possible GSJ special-issue proposal. Access: registration fee.

title: EURAM 2027 Annual Conference, VU Amsterdam, 22-25 June 2027 - paper deadline 12 January 2027
author_source: EURAM, conference website, 2026
note: Theme 'Rising Above: Embracing Resilience, Reimagining History, and Rethinking Management for a Sustainable Future'; submissions open late November 2026, deadline 12 January 2027 (14:00 CET), notification 11 March 2027; doctoral colloquium 21-22 June 2027 (deadline 19 January 2027); SIG tracks include International Management and Strategic Management with inter-organisational topics.
relevance: Second European outlet for an early version; EURAM's SIG structure allows a topic proposal on alliances and partnerships in geopolitically fragmented markets. Access: registration fee.

title: 43rd EGOS Colloquium, Liverpool, 8-10 July 2027 - sub-theme 57 'Where Networks Meet: Intra- and Inter-Organizational Networks' (short papers due 15 January 2027)
author_source: EGOS, call for short papers, 2026
note: Overall theme 'The Games We Play: Re-Writing the Rules of Organization?'; short-paper window early October 2026 to 15 January 2027 (12:00 CET); relevant sub-themes: ST57 'Where Networks Meet' (Stefan Breet, Stefano Tasselli) and ST41 'Intra- and inter-organizational networks and relationships in non-Western contexts' (Julia Brennecke, Christiana Weber, Jane Khayesi); also a sub-theme on meta-organizations.
relevance: Network and meta-organisation sub-themes are natural homes for a paper treating alliances as meta-organisations with differentiated member integration. Access: registration fee.

title: ECPR General Conference 2027, Universitat Pompeu Fabra Barcelona, 7-10 September 2027 (Section proposals from late October 2026)
author_source: ECPR, general conference page, 2026
note: Largest European political science meeting; call for Section proposals opens late October 2026, then Panel and Paper calls in early 2027; the Research Network on Differentiated Integration regularly runs Sections/Panels on DI (e.g. 'Differentiated Integration in Europe', 'Public Opinion and differentiated integration').
relevance: Venue to present the alliance application to the originators of the DI concept and recruit a political-science co-author; UACES 2027 (host still to be announced) is the alternative. Access: registration fee.

title: 2027 JIBS - National Taiwan University Paper Development Workshop, Taipei, 21 March 2027
author_source: AIB/JIBS, paper development workshop listing, 2026
note: JIBS PDW series offering developmental feedback from JIBS editors on full papers or proposals (2026 editions: SMU 2 March, Tsinghua 17 May, AIB Manchester 29 June, CUHK 5 December with proposals due 2 October 2026); the 2027 NTU workshop is scheduled for 21 March 2027 at the College of Management, Taipei (call and deadline to check on the AIB events list).
relevance: Direct route to editorial feedback on positioning a differentiated-integration alliance paper for JIBS; AIB 2027 Kuala Lumpur will also host a JIBS PDW. Access: free for accepted participants (travel).

title: Long Range Planning: Call for Special Issue Proposals (deadline 1 November 2026) and open calls
author_source: Long Range Planning, journal announcement, 2026
note: LRP invites proposals for special issues by 1 November 2026; current open SI 'Strategizing for Sustainable Business Model Innovation in the Digital Age' (deadline 31 August 2026, includes ecosystem collaboration). GSJ likewise accepts special-issue proposals (SMS 'Call for Proposals: Special Issues for GSJ') and JIBS lists an SI on 'AI, Data, and MNEs in a Multipolar World' (window 15-30 September 2027).
relevance: Opportunity to propose a special issue on 'differentiated integration in inter-organisational arrangements' bridging EU studies and strategy, rather than waiting for a fitting call; LRP and GSJ are both open to such proposals. Access: free to propose.

title: Global Strategy Journal Special Issue 'Globalizing Intelligence: Orchestrating Artificial Intelligence for Global Advantage' (submission window 15 September - 15 October 2026)
author_source: GSJ call for papers, 2026
note: Invites theoretical and empirical work on how AI shapes global competitiveness, strategy formation, international scaling and organisational change in MNEs; submissions 15 September to 15 October 2026. The SMS hub also lists GSJ's 'Global Innovation in an Era of Disruptive Changes' (closed) and the GSJ Idea and Paper Development Workshop series (SKEMA, April 2026).
relevance: Marginal but imminent: cross-border AI and data partnerships are a case of partners integrating different activities (data, models, compute) to different degrees under divergent national rules, i.e. differentiated integration in tech alliances. Access: open call.
